detail: The BY feed from the FUEL PUMP RELAY was CUT between R1 pin 7 and R166, and now drives the new 40A relay coil instead. Spliced UNDER THE REAR DRIVER SEAT
reason: Relay still switches on factory pump-on logic, but the FPCM is left with no supply
notes: Cut is on the BY run between R1 pin 7 and R122 pin 10. Whether it passes through an R166/R167 pair depends on an unresolved question - see WHICH FUEL PUMP DIAGRAM APPLIES. Either way the cut point and both endpoints are unchanged. Splice method not yet recorded

circuit: Fuel pump - factory control chain DEAD
wire: GR at the ECM, BY from the relay onward
detail: Factory chain: ECM connector D pin 15 (GR) commands the FUEL PUMP RELAY; the relay output (BY) runs B46 -> B97/R1 bulkhead (8-pin, area B-2) -> R122 pin 10 at the fuel pump controller. On STi-model cars an R166/R167 pair sits between R1 and R122 - see the diagram question
reason: Superseded by the hardwired relay
notes: Chain is INTACT up to R1 pin 7. Past the cut it feeds the new relay coil. R166/R167 and R122 carry nothing

detail: This circuit is BODY-SIDE wiring, and the body harness is 2004 WRX - so E/G(TB)-01 (WI-82, turbo) should govern, NOT the STi E/G(ST)-01 (WI-108). R166/R167 are indexed "(STi model)", meaning the STi CAR, not the STi engine. The 2005 STi ENGINE harness does not reach this circuit
reason: 2004 WRX body harness retained; only the engine harness is STi
notes: OPEN: Alan traced the run as passing through R166/R167, which a 2004 WRX body harness should not have. PHYSICALLY CHECK for an extra 6-pin connector pair between R1 and R122. If it is absent, the turbo diagram is correct and the cut is R1 pin 7 straight to R122 pin 10

connector: tap on the B wire spanning R58 pin 4 <-> R57 pin 16
detail: Pump ground leaves the pump on the OEM path at R58 pin 4. The black wire running from there to R57 pin 16 is tapped between the two connectors and grounded straight to CHASSIS UNDER THE REAR SEAT
reason: Gives the DW400 a short, local high-current return instead of the long factory run
notes: Factory wire toward R57 pin 16 is CUT, not paralleled - deliberate. GND-04 also carries the seat heaters, room/spot lights, door switches, rear accessory socket, fan control amp and compass mirror; DW400 current on that shared node would inject noise and shift the fuel level sender reference. TRADEOFF: the local chassis ground is now a SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE - clean bare metal, star washer, dielectric grease

detail: Factory pump ground per FSM GND-04 (WI-26) runs pump -> R58 pin 4 -> R57 pin 16 -> R15 pin 16 -> forward to the GND-04 ground point at the front of the car
reason: Superseded by the local chassis ground under the rear seat
notes: That run was sized for the stock pump. At DW400 current its length would cost real voltage at the pump, which is the point of the local ground. CUT at the tap - this path is open, not a parallel return

detail: Per FSM the black wire at R58 pin 4 is the common ground for the whole FUEL PUMP ASSEMBLY, which includes the fuel level sender
reason: Not a separate change - it rides on the pump ground tap
notes: So the sender now grounds locally under the rear seat too. SANITY CHECK: confirm the fuel gauge reads correctly at first start - a wrong or dead gauge would point here, not at the sender
